title: Epic: Hot-route capacity protection (tier-aware limits, priority routing, graceful degradation)
creator: Talia Benson
content:
Goal
Protect fleet health and preserve enterprise SLOs by preventing overload on a small number of hot, high-SLA routes (chat/completions, embeddings, rerank) from cascading into fleet-wide tail latency/5xx. This epic delivers tier-aware quotas/limits, priority admission/routing, and graceful degradation with consistent 429 semantics + observability.

Why now / motivating incident
We’ve had multiple burst events where best-effort/self-serve traffic on hot routes drove shared GPU pools into high p99 and elevated 5xx for enterprise tenants. The most actionable gap is the lack of deterministic admission control and tier budgets at the edges (gateway/routing) plus weak operator visibility when we start shedding.

In scope
- Gateway enforcement: tier-aware rate limits + quota evaluation; consistent 429 schema/headers/reason codes.
- Routing policy: priority classes, admission control under pressure, and controlled fallback (only where allowed).
- Fleet signals: integrate queue depth/scheduler lag + capacity signals into routing/policy decisions.
- Observability: per-route/per-tier metrics; overload activation events; SLO dashboards; alerting tuned to avoid paging storms on expected best-effort shedding.
- Operational readiness: runbooks, incident-bot notifications, game day, support macros and escalation paths.

Out of scope (explicit)
- Billing/pricing changes (only metadata hooks).
- Full scheduler rewrite (only integration points + signals needed for admission control).

Tier semantics (working)
- Enterprise: protected budgets with defined latency/availability targets; throttled last; no silent fallback unless explicitly allowed per-route/customer policy.
- Best-effort/self-serve: earlier and more predictable throttling under pressure; consistent 429s with clear retry/backoff guidance.

Milestones (target timeline; adjust as we learn)
1) Discovery + requirements (Done)
   - Identify protected routes + route groups; top tenants + traffic shapes; existing pain points.
   - Confirm initial priority classes and SLO mapping.

2) Design + ADR (Done)
   - Decide enforcement points (gateway vs routing vs runtime), policy evaluation contract, and 429 semantics.

3) MVP implementation (In Progress)
   - Tier-aware gateway rate limits + quota evaluation.
   - Policy engine priority class evaluation and deterministic decision logging.
   - Routing admission control driven by runtime/fleet signals.
   - Initial dashboards in one region (us-east) and allowlisted enterprise accounts.

4) Game day + canary rollout (Planned)
   - Simulate burst traffic on protected hot route(s).
   - Validate: enterprise p95/p99 and error budget burn stays within thresholds; best-effort shedding occurs before fleet degradation.
   - Tune alerts and thresholds; confirm 429 semantics for streaming clients.

5) GA + hardening (Planned)
   - Multi-region rollout; finalize runbooks/support playbooks.
   - Remove legacy throttling path after stability period.
   - Post-launch metrics review + follow-up tickets.

Owners / key stakeholders
- Exec sponsors: Priya Natarajan (Platform), Neha Kapoor (Reliability)
- Program mgmt: Talia Benson
- Product: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API tier semantics)
- Eng leads: Ethan Park (control plane enforcement), Mina Haddad (smart routing), Jordan Lee (policy engine), Mateo Alvarez / Sofia Ivanova (runtime scheduling integration)
- SRE: Rafael Mendes (overload protection + gameday), Aisha Bello (error budgets + alert tuning)
- Support readiness: Dev Patel (support lead), Liam O’Rourke (TAM rollout liaison)

Success metrics
- Reduction in fleet-wide Sev1/Sev2 incidents attributable to hot-route overload (target: materially reduced; report post-launch).
- Enterprise protected routes: meet defined availability/latency SLO during simulated and real bursts; reduced p99 spikes vs baseline.
- Best-effort traffic: predictable 429 rates under pressure; fewer opaque 5xx/timeout failures.
- Operator experience: clear overload activation signals, dashboards, and runbook flow; incident-bot notifications actionable.

Implementation notes / constraints
- Data-plane overhead must remain low; avoid high-cardinality policy checks and tags.
- Decisions must be deterministic and auditable for enterprise escalations.
- Rollout must be reversible: feature flags, region-by-region enablement, account allowlists, safe defaults.

Related implementation tickets (tracked under this epic)
- ENG-4922 API gateway tier-aware rate limiter
- ENG-4923 Policy engine: priority classes + route budgets + deterministic logging
- ENG-4924 Routing: integrate capacity signals for admission control
- ENG-4925 Runtime: export queue depth + scheduler lag metrics
- ENG-4926 SRE dashboards + alerts
- ENG-4927 Incident-bot notifications when protection activates
- ENG-4928 Feature flags + progressive rollout guardrails
- ENG-4929 Load test plan + game day execution
- ENG-4930 Support playbook + 429 docs
- ENG-4931 Post-launch metrics review + follow-ups

Open questions / risks
- Threshold selection: we need stable, low-noise capacity signals (queue depth vs GPU saturation) and region-specific tuning.
- Fallback guardrails: which enterprise routes may fallback (model/region) vs strict admission control; avoid silent quality changes.
- Streaming semantics: ensure consistent termination behavior when shedding occurs (customer debuggability).
- Cardinality: overload reason metrics must remain bounded; validate tags before GA.

Rollout plan (initial)
- us-east canary with allowlisted enterprise accounts on protected routes.
- Expand to eu-west after 1–2 weeks of stable canary metrics.
- GA enablement with go/no-go gates: enterprise SLO stability, acceptable shed behavior for best-effort, alert noise within bounds, support readiness complete.

Notes for on-call/support
- New 429s are expected for best-effort under pressure. Enterprise 429s should trigger immediate investigation using reason codes and the overload dashboards; escalate to on-call + TAM only if enterprise protected routes exceed agreed thresholds or behavior deviates from documented policy.
comments: 2025-12-03 (Talia Benson): Kicked off cross-team sync. Action: Platform to propose initial route groups; SRE to provide SLO targets by tier for /v1/chat/completions and embeddings first.

2025-12-10 (Ravi Menon): Proposed enforcement split: gateway for quota/rate-limit, routing for admission control using queue depth + scheduler lag. Runtime only exports signals (no per-request policy logic). Captured in ADR draft.

2025-12-18 (Allison Grant): Please keep overload event metrics low-cardinality. Avoid tagging by customer_id on the hot path. Route group + tier + reason_code should be sufficient for dashboards; customer drill-down via logs/debug endpoint only.
2026-01-06 (Ethan Park): MVP landing in us-east behind flag with allowlist. Need final PM sign-off on enterprise vs best-effort 429 copy + headers (DES-214).

2026-01-14 (Rafael Mendes): Game day readiness: we’ll run a burst on chat route using load harness. Success criteria: enterprise p99 < target and error budget burn stays under paging threshold while best-effort shed rate increases. Scheduling dry-run booked for next week.
2026-01-28 (Dev Patel): Support asks for a short internal FAQ: how to interpret overload vs quota 429 reason codes and when to request an exception. Tracking under ENG-4930.
